notes: §1985:VI.5.15.5 GR2: 'Format 2 can be used only in connection with condition-names' and 'Wherever the THRU phrase is used, literal-2 must be less than literal-3.' BindEntry refuses the THRU phrase on a non-88 entry (ConditionOnlyPhraseOf, COBOL2167), and BindCondition calls CheckRangesAscending, which compares the two ends in the program collating sequence fixed at compile time (COBOL2961); the gap of the prior PARTIAL (figurative constants, ALL literals and symbolic-characters skipped) is closed: those ends are now compared too. Probed at --std 85: (d) HIGH-VALUE THRU LOW-VALUE, SPACE THRU SPACE, "Z" THRU SPACE, QUOTE THRU SPACE, ZERO THRU SPACE on PIC X, ALL "Z" THRU ALL "A", symbolic-characters SC2 THRU SC1, "ABC" THRU "AB", 9 THRU 1, -5 THRU -10 and 1.5 THRU 1.25 on S99V99 all refused; SPACE THRU "Z", LOW-VALUE THRU HIGH-VALUE, "AB" THRU "ABC", -10 THRU -5 and -1.5 THRU 1.25 accepted; "a" THRU "A" refused in the native sequence and accepted (and true for "a") under PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE EBCDIC; (b) VALUE 1 THRU 2 on a level 01 refused COBOL2167. Classes a, c, e, f do not reach this rule. The witness is the refusal of 9 THRU 1 on a PIC 99 item. History: until the 1985 re-read 5 (2026-11-14) this row read PARTIAL, naming no kb/Work note; the re-read of main dc1f2dcce8 found that defect fixed by the landing of kb/Work PB5181 and records CONFORMS, upheld by an independent refuter (code read: op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-05.json, refuter op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-05-refute.json).

next.reason: 1985: 'Format 2 can be used only in connection with condition-names ... Wherever the THRU phrase is used, literal-2 must be less than literal-3.' The first sentence is kept: §2023:13.18.63.3 SR33 'Formats 3 and 5 may be specified only when the level-number of the subject of the entry is 88.' The ordering requirement is narrowed: §2023:13.18.63.3 SR26 keeps 'literal-2 shall be less than the value of literal-3' unconditionally only for classes other than alphanumeric or national; for alphanumeric or national literals it applies only 'when the runtime collating sequence is known', and 'The runtime collating sequence is unknown when the collating sequence is defined by a locale or ... otherwise determined at runtime'. A THRU range 1985 refused can therefore be accepted. Looser, not an exception condition.
